source: Extracted from RAI ARC assets (registry.html + ARC v1.1 per-type classification tools). Verbatim strings; do not paraphrase. Autonomy levels use the paper's L1-L5 scale with the Section 2.4 verbatim definitions (Feng et al.'s five-level framework as quoted in arXiv:2607.09586; old 1/2/3 -> L1/L3/L5, see ADR-0017).
scale: Each dimension scored 1/2/3 (Tier 1 Low / Tier 2 Medium / Tier 3 High).

risk_tier_defs.1: Tier 1 — Low. All twelve dimensions at baseline. Standard documentation and acceptable-use controls.
risk_tier_defs.2: Tier 2 — Medium. Elevated dimensions but none at the highest level. Enhanced oversight, documented controls, periodic review.
risk_tier_defs.3: Tier 3 — High. At least one dimension at its highest level (worst-case-wins). Comprehensive governance: executive approval, real-time monitoring, kill-switch capability, pre-deployment testing.

autonomy_level_defs.1: Level 1 — Operator. The user directs all of the agent's actions, while the agent acts on command.
autonomy_level_defs.2: Level 2 — Collaborator. The user and the agent collaboratively plan and execute actions.
autonomy_level_defs.3: Level 3 — Consultant. The agent leads the actions, but consults the user for expertise and preferences.
autonomy_level_defs.4: Level 4 — Approver. The agent engages the user only in situations where they require a green-light in specified risk scenarios.
autonomy_level_defs.5: Level 5 — Observer. The agent has full autonomy, whereas the user only has the ability to monitor.

rollup_rule_stated: worst-case-wins: any dimension at 3 -> Tier 3; else max 2 or average >= 1.5 -> Tier 2; else Tier 1.
